questions.stem: Dana is the salaried on-site manager of an apartment building and shows vacant units and takes rental applications as part of her customary duties. She has no real estate license. Which statement is correct?
choices: Dana needs a license because showing units and taking applications are leasing activities
Dana is exempt only if she shows fewer than ten units in a calendar year
Dana is exempt as a salaried on-site manager performing customary duties
Dana must be supervised by an employing broker but does not need her own license
questions.explanation: Colorado exempts a salaried on-site manager of an apartment building or condominium who is doing customary duties. There is no unit-count limit in the exemption.

questions.stem: A broker wants to qualify as an employing broker so she can hire other brokers. Which requirement applies?
choices: Two years of active practice in the prior five years, an experience point requirement, and a 24-hour Brokerage Administration course
Two years of Active licensure as an associate broker, with no further coursework
One year of Active licensure and passing the state portion of the exam a second time
Five years as an independent broker and a written recommendation from her current employing broker
questions.explanation: An employing broker needs two years of active practice in the prior five years, must meet an experience point requirement, and must complete a 24-hour Brokerage Administration course. Two years of Active licensure alone qualifies a broker only for independent status.

questions.stem: A newly approved broker applicant receives the Commission's notice but does not provide proof of E&O insurance or the name of an employing broker within 30 days. What happens?
choices: The application is denied and the applicant must retake the exam
The license is issued Active for 90 days while coverage is obtained
The applicant must restart the 168-hour pre-licensing education
The license is issued Inactive
questions.explanation: If proof of E&O coverage or an employing broker isn't provided within 30 days of the Commission's notice, the license is issued Inactive. The broker can't do licensed work until the license is Active.

questions.stem: The only employing broker of a small Colorado brokerage firm suddenly leaves. What relief can the Division director provide while the firm finds a replacement?
choices: A temporary license for up to 90 days, with one extension of up to 90 days for good cause
Permission for the senior associate broker to act as employing broker indefinitely
A one-year waiver of supervision requirements for all associates
Nothing; the firm must stop all brokerage activity until the Commission approves a successor
questions.explanation: The Division director can issue a temporary license for up to 90 days, with one extension of up to 90 days for good cause, while the firm finds a new employing broker.

questions.stem: How many hours of approved pre-licensing education must a Colorado broker applicant complete (unless the applicant holds a college degree with a real estate major)?
choices: 48 hours
72 hours
168 hours
120 hours
questions.explanation: Colorado requires 168 hours: 48 hours of real estate law and practice, 48 hours of Colorado contracts and regulations, and 72 hours of trust accounts, closings, legal issues, and practical applications. 48 and 72 are only components of the total.

questions.stem: Which Colorado broker must maintain a place of business in Colorado?
choices: An associate broker who works from home for a Denver firm
An inactive broker who lives in Colorado
An independent broker who lives in Colorado
An associate broker whose employing broker has several branch offices
questions.explanation: Independent and employing brokers who live in Colorado must maintain a Colorado place of business. Associate brokers and inactive brokers are exempt.

questions.stem: A broker's first Colorado license is issued on October 15, 2026. When does it expire?
choices: October 15, 2027
December 31, 2026
December 31, 2029
October 15, 2029
questions.explanation: A new license expires at midnight on December 31 of the year it was issued, regardless of the issue date. After that, licenses run on three-year calendar cycles.

questions.stem: How many hours of continuing education must an active Colorado broker complete in each three-year license cycle?
choices: 12 hours, all from the Annual Commission Update
24 hours, including the 4-hour Annual Commission Update each year
36 hours, including 12 hours of contracts
24 hours of electives chosen by the broker, with no required courses
questions.explanation: Colorado requires 24 CE hours per three-year cycle. Twelve come from the 4-hour Annual Commission Update taken every year, and the other 12 are Commission-approved electives.

questions.stem: An active broker skipped the Annual Commission Update in the first year of her cycle and wants to take two versions in year two to catch up. What is the rule?
choices: She may take both versions in year two as long as she finishes before renewal
She may substitute 4 extra elective hours for the missed update course
She can't make up the missed course and must use an alternative such as the 24-hour Broker Reactivation course
She is excused because the update course is required only in the final year of the cycle
questions.explanation: A missed year's Annual Commission Update can't be made up later. A broker who falls short must use an alternative, such as a 24-hour Broker Reactivation course, passing the state exam, or completing 72 hours of contracts/regulations and closings coursework.

questions.stem: A broker's license expired on December 31, and he applies to reinstate it six months later. What must he pay?
choices: Only the regular renewal fee
The renewal fee plus a reinstatement fee equal to half the renewal fee
The renewal fee plus a reinstatement fee equal to the full renewal fee
Nothing until he retakes the exam as a new applicant
questions.explanation: More than 31 days but no more than one year after expiration, reinstatement costs the renewal fee plus a reinstatement fee of half the renewal fee. The full-fee reinstatement charge applies after one year, up to three years.

questions.stem: Marco placed his license on inactive status after leaving his firm. Which statement about his inactive license is correct?
choices: He must keep carrying E&O insurance while inactive
He no longer needs to renew the license or pay renewal fees
He may continue to show property as long as he does not write contracts
His former employing broker may still pay him commissions earned while he was Active
questions.explanation: An inactive broker can still be paid by a former employing broker for commissions earned while Active. Inactive brokers must still renew and pay fees, don't need E&O, and can't do anything that requires a license.

questions.stem: A broker enters a no contest plea to a criminal charge. What must the broker do?
choices: Give the Commission written notice within 30 calendar days
Report it at the next license renewal
Notify the Commission only if the plea results in a conviction
Notify the employing broker, who reports it to the Commission annually
questions.explanation: A broker must give the Commission written notice within 30 calendar days of a conviction or a guilty or no contest plea; deferred judgments count too. Waiting for renewal or for a conviction is too late.

questions.stem: A broker is shopping for an independent E&O policy instead of the Division's group plan. Which policy meets Colorado's minimum terms for individual coverage?
choices: $50,000 per claim, $150,000 aggregate, $500 deductible
$100,000 per claim, $300,000 aggregate, $1,000 deductible
$100,000 per claim, $300,000 aggregate, $2,500 deductible
$100,000 per claim, $200,000 aggregate, $1,000 deductible
questions.explanation: Individual coverage must be at least $100,000 per claim and $300,000 annual aggregate, with a deductible of no more than $1,000 per occurrence. A $2,500 deductible is too high, and a $200,000 aggregate is too low.

questions.stem: An active broker forgets to pay his E&O premium and the coverage lapses. What happens to his license?
choices: It stays Active for a 30-day grace period
It is automatically revoked
It goes Inactive immediately
It expires at the end of the current renewal cycle
questions.explanation: If E&O coverage lapses, or the broker fails to certify continuing coverage, the license goes Inactive immediately. Doing brokerage while uninsured is acting on an inactive license.

questions.stem: A broker's license has been inactive for four years and she wants to reactivate it. Which option satisfies the education or testing requirement?
choices: Completing only the current year's Annual Commission Update
Passing the state portion of the exam
Completing 12 hours of elective CE
Showing proof of E&O coverage alone
questions.explanation: When a license has been inactive for more than three years, reactivation requires passing the state exam or completing 72 hours of coursework (48 hours of contracts and regulations plus 24 hours of closings).

questions.stem: A seller asks a Colorado broker to take a net listing at $400,000, with the broker keeping anything above that. Which statement best reflects Colorado's position?
choices: Net listings are illegal in Colorado, and the broker would lose the license for taking one
Net listings are allowed only on the Commission-approved net listing form
They aren't expressly prohibited but are discouraged, mainly because of secret-profit risk
Net listings are permitted only for commercial property
questions.explanation: Colorado's statute and current Commission rules don't expressly prohibit net listings, but the Commission discourages them. There is no Commission-approved net listing form, and a broker who uses one to take an undisclosed profit can be disciplined for secret compensation.

questions.stem: After a residential sale, a firm believes the seller still owes part of its commission. Before filing a lien or lis pendens against the property, the firm must:
choices: Obtain a court judgment
File a complaint with the Commission so it can decide the dispute
Give the seller 10 days' written notice
Get the buyer's written consent
questions.explanation: In residential deals, a firm can't file a lien or lis pendens or otherwise cloud title to collect a disputed commission without first getting a court judgment. The Commission doesn't decide money disputes; those go to court or arbitration.

questions.stem: A sale closed on August 15, 2026. Under Colorado's record retention rule, until at least what date must the broker keep the transaction file?
choices: August 15, 2029
August 15, 2030
August 15, 2031
December 31, 2029
questions.explanation: Required records must be kept for four years, starting from the date the transaction closed. Three- and five-year periods are common distractors.

questions.stem: A firm stores all its transaction files electronically. During a Commission audit, the server crashes and the broker can't retrieve the files. Which statement is correct?
choices: The broker is excused until the system is repaired, however long that takes
The broker may substitute a written summary of each transaction
Electronic storage is not allowed for trust account records, so the firm is already in violation
A technical problem is not an excuse; the broker must still produce the records
questions.explanation: Records may be kept electronically, but they must stay retrievable and legibly printable for four years, and a technical problem with the storage system is not an excuse for failing to produce them. Trust account records may also be kept electronically.

questions.stem: Who can require a broker to produce electronic or printed copies of a transaction's required records?
choices: Only the Commission
The Commission or any principal party to the transaction
Only the broker's employing broker
Any member of the public
questions.explanation: Electronic or printed copies must be produced when the Commission or any principal party to the transaction asks.

questions.stem: A broker receives notice of a complaint that she is sure has no merit, so she ignores the Commission's response deadline. What is the likely result?
choices: Nothing, because the complaint will be dismissed anyway
The complaint is automatically transferred to small claims court
She can face discipline for failing to respond on time, even if the complaint lacks merit
Her employing broker must answer for her, and she has no further obligation
questions.explanation: A broker notified of a complaint or audit must respond in writing by the Commission's deadline, addressing each allegation and including the complete transaction file. Failing to respond on time is itself grounds for discipline, even if the complaint has no merit.

questions.stem: After closing, which item does the Commission NOT require a broker to keep in the transaction file?
choices: The buyer's loan application
The signed contract to buy and sell
The brokerage disclosure
The closing statement
questions.explanation: A broker isn't required to obtain and keep copies of loan applications, title commitments, existing public records, lender-required disclosures, or related affirmations from an independent closing entity after closing. Contracts, brokerage disclosures, and closing statements are on the Transaction File Checklist.

questions.stem: Which record must a firm keep for each beneficiary of a trust account, showing receipts and disbursements with no negative balance?
choices: The journal
The deposit agreement
The accounting control policy
The ledger
questions.explanation: A ledger is kept for each beneficiary, shows the same details as the journal, and may never have a negative balance. The journal is a single chronological record of all receipts and disbursements for the account.

questions.stem: An associate broker moves from Firm A to Firm B. Who is responsible for keeping the transaction files from his deals at Firm A?
choices: Only Firm A, because listings belong to the firm
Only the Commission, which takes custody of files when a broker transfers
The broker himself remains responsible for keeping those files
No one, because files may be destroyed once a broker transfers
questions.explanation: A broker stays responsible for keeping their transaction files even after moving to a new brokerage. Each broker and brokerage keeps a transaction file for every transaction.

questions.stem: A broker exchanged dozens of emails and texts with a buyer during a transaction. Under Division guidance, which statement is correct?
choices: They must be printed and kept for four years
Keeping them is recommended but not required
They must be deleted after closing to protect privacy
They must be sent to the Commission at closing
questions.explanation: The Division recommends, but does not require, keeping related emails and texts. The required file contents are listed on the Commission's Transaction File Checklist, and a firm may require more.
